courses.title: Cross-model 1 · Solid to SubD and back
courses.objective: Turn a solid into a soft SubD shape, smooth it, and turn it back into a solid.
courses.challenge: Convert the block, set smoothness to 3, convert it back.

steps.title: Make a practice block
steps.learn: You need a solid to start from. This lesson uses a plain block 60 by 40 mm and 30 mm tall. It could just as well come from the Form workspace, a boolean or an imported file.
instructions: Press Do it for me. Aakar draws the block.
Or build your own: a rectangle extruded 30 mm.
steps.why: Every shape can move between model types. A solid is the usual starting point.

checkpoint.expected: A block appears in the 3D view.

steps.recovery: Nothing appeared? Press Do it for me again.

guide.now: Press “Do it for me” to make the block.

steps.title: Turn the block into a SubD shape
steps.learn: Solid to SubD replaces the solid with an editable cage: a few points you can move, extrude or crease. Every SubD tool now works on it. You can also just press a SubD tool while a solid is selected and Aakar converts it for you.
instructions: Open the Model tab, find the Convert group, press Solid to SubD.
Or press Do it for me.
steps.why: SubD tools only edit SubD shapes. This is the bridge that lets them edit any solid.

checkpoint.expected: The block is now a smooth cage.

steps.recovery: Nothing happened? Click the block first so it is selected.

steps.title: Make it smoother
steps.learn: Smoothness is how many times the cage is rounded off. Level 3 gives a soft pillow.
instructions: Switch to the SubD tab, press Level and choose 3.
Or press Do it for me.
steps.why: Smoothness is a number you can change any time.

checkpoint.expected: The block looks like a rounded pillow.

steps.recovery: Still sharp? Check the level is 3, not 0.

steps.title: Turn it back into a solid
steps.learn: To solid makes a normal solid from the smooth shape, so you can use Round, Shell, booleans and drawings.
instructions: Press To solid in the SubD tab.
Or press Do it for me.
steps.why: Finished shapes usually go back to a solid for making.
steps.recovery: No solid? The SubD must be closed.

steps.title: Solid and SubD are linked
steps.learn: Solid to SubD makes a cage any SubD tool can edit; To solid brings it back. Curved faces become smooth surfaces, so exact holes and fillets are not kept.
instructions: Read the summary, then press Got it.
steps.why: A short recap helps the idea stick.

checkpoint.expected: You can say which tool moves a shape between solid, SubD and NURBS.

steps.recovery: Want to see it again? Press Start again.

guide.cap: Done. Solid to SubD makes a cage any SubD tool can edit; To solid brings it back. Curved faces become smooth surfaces, so exact holes and fillets are not kept.

courses.title: Cross-model 2 · NURBS surface to SubD and back
courses.objective: Turn an exact NURBS surface into an editable SubD cage, then back into exact patches.
courses.challenge: Loft a vase, convert it to SubD, convert it back to NURBS.

steps.title: Make a lofted surface
steps.learn: A loft joins several outlines into one smooth NURBS surface. This lesson lofts five circles of different sizes into a vase.
instructions: Press Do it for me. Aakar draws the circles and lofts them.
steps.why: NURBS surfaces are exact but hard to push around freely.
steps.recovery: Nothing? Press Do it for me again.

guide.now: Press “Do it for me” to loft the vase.

steps.title: Turn the surface into a SubD cage
steps.learn: NURBS to SubD samples the surface into a cage that follows it closely. Open edges stay sharp. Now you can edit it with soft SubD tools.
instructions: Open the Model tab, Convert group, press NURBS to SubD.
Or press Do it for me.
steps.why: SubD is easier to reshape freely than NURBS control points.

checkpoint.expected: A SubD copy of the vase appears.

steps.recovery: Select the surface first if nothing happens.

steps.title: Turn the SubD back into NURBS
steps.learn: To NURBS makes bicubic patches. They are exact on regular areas and within a set tolerance elsewhere.
instructions: Open the SubD tab and press To NURBS.
Or press Do it for me.
steps.why: Manufacturing and exchange files want exact surfaces.

checkpoint.expected: A set of NURBS patches appears.

steps.recovery: It can take a few seconds on large cages.

steps.title: NURBS and SubD are linked
steps.learn: NURBS to SubD for free reshaping; SubD to NURBS for exact output. The round trip is an approximation, not an identical surface.
instructions: Read the summary, then press Got it.
steps.why: A short recap helps the idea stick.

checkpoint.expected: You can say which tool moves a shape between solid, SubD and NURBS.

steps.recovery: Want to see it again? Press Start again.

guide.cap: Done. NURBS to SubD for free reshaping; SubD to NURBS for exact output. The round trip is an approximation, not an identical surface.

courses.title: Cross-model 3 · A surface from a solid face
courses.objective: Copy a face of a solid as a surface sheet, then make the whole solid a SubD.
courses.challenge: Copy the top face as a surface.

steps.title: Make a practice block
steps.learn: You need a solid to start from. This lesson uses a plain block 60 by 40 mm and 30 mm tall. It could just as well come from the Form workspace, a boolean or an imported file.
instructions: Press Do it for me. Aakar draws the block.
Or build your own: a rectangle extruded 30 mm.
steps.why: Every shape can move between model types. A solid is the usual starting point.

checkpoint.expected: A block appears in the 3D view.

steps.recovery: Nothing appeared? Press Do it for me again.

guide.now: Press “Do it for me” to make the block.

steps.title: Click the top face
steps.learn: A surface is a face with no thickness. Pick the top face to copy it.
instructions: Click the top face. It turns orange.
Or press Do it for me.
steps.why: Surface from solid copies the faces you pick.

steps.title: Make a surface of it
steps.learn: Surface from solid copies the picked faces as a zero-thickness sheet that follows the solid when it changes. Curved faces become fine triangles, so it is a mesh sheet, not an exact NURBS sheet.
instructions: Model tab, Convert group, press Surface from solid.
Or press Do it for me.
steps.why: Surfaces can be used for trimming, splitting and shelling.

checkpoint.expected: A thin sheet lies on top of the block.

steps.recovery: Choose “The faces I picked” in the dialog.

steps.title: You can lift a surface off a solid
steps.learn: Pick faces, press Surface from solid. For an exact NURBS version of a whole solid, use Solid to SubD, then SubD › To NURBS.
instructions: Read the summary, then press Got it.
steps.why: A short recap helps the idea stick.

checkpoint.expected: You can say which tool moves a shape between solid, SubD and NURBS.

steps.recovery: Want to see it again? Press Start again.

guide.cap: Done. Pick faces, press Surface from solid. For an exact NURBS version of a whole solid, use Solid to SubD, then SubD › To NURBS.

courses.title: Cross-model 4 · A face as an exact NURBS surface
courses.objective: Turn the top face of a block with a hole into an exact NURBS surface that keeps its hole.
courses.challenge: Convert the top face, then the wall of the hole.

steps.title: Make the practice block
steps.learn: This lesson uses a block 60 by 40 mm and 20 mm tall with a round hole 16 mm across.
instructions: Press Do it for me. Aakar draws the block and cuts the hole.
steps.why: A flat face with a hole is the classic test for an exact surface.

checkpoint.expected: A block with a round hole appears.

steps.recovery: Nothing appeared? Press Do it for me again.

guide.now: Press “Do it for me” to make the block with the hole.

steps.title: Click the top face
steps.learn: The top face is flat and has a round hole in it.
instructions: Click the face in the 3D view. It turns orange.
Or press Do it for me and Aakar picks it.
steps.why: Direct editing always starts with the face you want to change.
steps.recovery: Not orange? Click it again. A face is a flat or round side of the part, not an edge.

guide.now: Click the top face of the block in the 3D view.

steps.title: Make an exact NURBS surface
steps.learn: Face to NURBS builds a true NURBS surface. The flat top becomes one exact patch trimmed by its outline, so the hole stays a real hole. Round hole walls become exact rational cylinders. Cones, spheres and free-form faces are not converted.
instructions: Model tab, Convert group, press Face to NURBS.
Or press Do it for me.
steps.why: Exact surfaces can be used in surface tools and exported without turning into triangles.

checkpoint.expected: A NURBS surface lies on the top face.

steps.recovery: Pick a flat or cylindrical face. Other curved faces say why they cannot convert.

steps.title: You can make exact NURBS from faces
steps.learn: Pick faces, press Face to NURBS. Flat faces keep their holes; cylinders become exact surfaces.
instructions: Read the summary, then press Got it.
steps.why: A short recap helps the idea stick.

checkpoint.expected: You can say which tool moves a shape between solid, SubD and NURBS.

steps.recovery: Want to see it again? Press Start again.

guide.cap: Done. Pick faces, press Face to NURBS. Flat faces keep their holes; cylinders become exact surfaces.
